What the run found (Aristotle's summary, paraphrased; not machine-checked):
- The split is the one the record's own decomposition already makes; the join (case split on k*k <= n, union of two finite sets) was written but not compiled anywhere.
- n >= k^2: Ecklund (1969) gives a prime factor <= n/k except (62, 6); settled o…

route.text: Split by k*k <= n (Ecklund's range) against 2k <= n < k*k, each a finiteness claim, joined by Set.Finite.union.

justification.text: k is non-zero: 0 < k is a conjunct of the same set predicate. Nat floor division matches the informal max(n/k, k): for a natural number p, p > floor(n/k) holds exactly when p > n/k.
